title: Find if Path Exists in Graph
summary: Given a bi-directional graph with vertices labeled from 0 to n-1 and edges represented as a 2D integer array, where each edge is denoted by [ui, vi] indicating a bi-directional connection between vertex ui and vertex vi, determine if there is a valid path from the source vertex to the destination vertex.
statement: Given a bi-directional graph with vertices labeled from 0 to n-1 and edges represented as a 2D integer array, where each edge is denoted by [ui, vi] indicating a bi-directional connection between vertex ui and vertex vi, determine if there is a valid path from the source vertex to the destination vertex. Return true if such a path exists, otherwise return false.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; vertices are numbered 0 through n-1.
edges contains undirected connections and has at most 200000 entries.
Return whether source and destination belong to the same connected component.
hints: Reachability asks whether the destination is in the source connected component.
Build both directions, then traverse while recording visited vertices.
Push source; repeatedly pop, return on destination, and push each unseen neighbor.
Traversal reaches exactly the vertices connected by a path; the visited set bounds each vertex to one expansion.
editorial: Traversal reaches exactly the vertices connected by a path; the visited set bounds each vertex to one expansion.

tests.explanation: Every vertex lies in one cycle, so zero can reach two.
The endpoints lie in separate components, so no path exists.
